findings.detail: `fallback = applyDefaults ? (defaultFor(key) ?? '') : ''` sits inside the per-row loop, and `defaultFor` runs `normalizeHeader` — four regex replaces plus a toLowerCase — on the same fixed set of template headers for every row. The header set is invariant across rows, so the work is rows × columns when it only needs to be columns: a 43-column Simple template over 500 extracted rows is ~21,500 redundant normalisations. No user-visible impact at realistic OCR volumes (rows come from images, not a spreadsheet), which is why this is low rather than a hot-path finding — it would rise to medium only if this mapper were ever reused for the sheet-sized inputs the other tabs handle.
findings.summary: defaultFor() re-normalises every template header once per row instead of once per column

findings.detail: The diff rewrites this function body entirely, so its `rows: any[]` parameter is newly-added code rather than a line the PR merely reindents — the type-safety handbook's carve-out for untouched legacy lines doesn't apply. The wrapper now adds nothing: it forwards all three arguments to mapRowsToTemplate unchanged, so the only thing it contributes is an `any` that erases the `TemplateRow` typing the new module was written to provide. Concretely, a caller passing the wrong shape (e.g. simpleRows before the Simple/Variable split at line 558) type-checks silently here but would not against mapRowsToTemplate's own signature.
findings.summary: Rewritten mapDataToTemplate keeps `any[]` and is now a pure pass-through alias
